title: The Iron Age
summary: The Iron Age is the archaeological period that follows the Bronze Age, marked by iron gradually replacing bronze as the main metal for tools and weapons. Iron objects appeared in Iran and Mesopotamia as early as the 12th century BCE, while in Europe the period typically started around 800 BCE; in Britain it closed with the Roman invasion of 43 CE. European archaeologists divide it into the early Hallstatt and later La Tène periods.

uncertainty.note: Start is the earliest regional beginning cited (Near East, 1200 BCE); Europe begins around 800 BCE and later regions later still. End is the Roman invasion of Britain in 43 CE, the conventional close in north-western Europe.

as_recorded.value: about 800 BC to the Roman invasion of 43 AD

where.modern_name: Hallstatt, Upper Austria, Austria (proxy pin: the site named in the early Iron Age period; the period has no single location)
where.note: Pin is Hallstatt, the type site of the early European Iron Age Hallstatt culture, and stands as a proxy for a period that spans Europe, the Near East and beyond.

importance.justification: The transition to iron tooling that underpinned later classical societies, and the periodisation that gives archaeology much of its basic chronology.

related.because: Iron objects appeared in Iran and Mesopotamia as early as the 12th century BCE, during the upheaval of the Late Bronze Age collapse.
Roman conquest closes the Iron Age in Britain and much of western Europe.
